response.sql: WITH o AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS a FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark HAVING COUNT(remaincount) > 0), ov AS (SELECT AVG(remaincount) AS v FROM orderexecutions), g AS (SELECT o.ordersmark, o.a, o.a - ov.v AS ex1 FROM o, ov WHERE o.a > ov.v), g2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m FROM g), f AS (SELECT g.a, g.ex1, g.a - g2.m AS ex2 FROM g, g2 WHERE g.a > g2.m) SELECT AVG(a) AS avg_of_order_avgs, AVG(ex1) AS avg_excess_over_overall, AVG(ex2) AS avg_excess_over_group_avg FROM f

assumptions.assumption: The 'overall average unfilled quantity' is the average of remaincount across all execution rows (NULLs ignored), not the average of the per-order averages.
Executions with NULL ordersmark form a single group (GROUP BY puts NULLs together), and that group is treated as one order.

The 'group's own average' is the average of the per-order averages among orders above the overall average; only orders strictly above it are kept. Orders whose remaincount is entirely NULL have no average and are excluded.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average is the mean of the per-order averages (each order weighted equally) rather than the mean over all execution rows.
